Traditional Swiss Rösti

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Rösti is a classic Swiss dish made primarily from grated potatoes, traditionally enjoyed as a hearty breakfast or side dish. It is especially popular during Berchtoldstag, a Swiss holiday celebrated on January 2nd, where families gather to enjoy comforting, rustic foods that warm the winter day.

Ingredients

  • 2 lbs (900 g) potatoes, preferably waxy
  • 2 tbsp (30 ml) butter or clarified butter
  • Salt, to taste
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • Optional: 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • Optional: 1/2 cup (50 g) grated Swiss cheese

Method

  1. Parboil the potatoes in their skins for about 10 minutes until just tender but still firm.
  2. Drain and let the potatoes cool completely, preferably overnight in the refrigerator to dry out.
  3. Peel the cooled potatoes and coarsely grate them using a box grater or food processor.
  4. If using onion, sauté it in a little butter until translucent and mix into the grated potatoes.
  5. Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat and melt 1 tablespoon of butter.
  6. Add the grated potatoes, pressing them down evenly into a flat cake about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick.
  7. Cook undisturbed for 10-15 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.
  8. Carefully flip the rösti using a plate or lid to help invert it, then slide it back into the pan to cook the other side with the remaining butter for another 10-15 minutes.
  9. Season with salt and pepper to taste and add cheese on top during the last few minutes if desired, allowing it to melt.
  10. Serve hot as a side dish or with eggs for a traditional Berchtoldstag breakfast.

Tips

  • Use waxy potatoes like Yukon Gold for the best texture and flavor.
  • For extra crispiness, avoid stirring the rösti while it cooks and press it firmly into the pan.
  • Add herbs like fresh thyme or chives for a fragrant variation.
